notes:
PRIORITY 1 — write-response fidelity (echo vs storage), tested across TWO separate writes: Write 1 set assignee null→'ing@bsstag.com' and run_state new_run→in_progress. Its 200 body echoed assignee as null (the OLD value, not what was just set), overall_progress as {Untested:4} (storage held 5), and a fresh updated_at of 07:16:59.000Z. A fresh get_test_run_v2 immediately after showed assignee='ing@bsstag.com' (correctly applied in storage), overall_progress={Untested:5}, and updated_at UNCHANGED at 06:27:38.743Z (the write never advanced it). Write 2 set description→'update-probe-second-description' and run_state→under_review (omitting assignee/tags). Its 200 body again echoed overall_progress={Untested:4} vs storage's {Untested:5}, and a fresh updated_at of 07:17:37.000Z vs storage's still-unchanged 06:27:38.743Z; description and run_state were echoed correctly this time (both changed and matched storage). VERDICT ON THE PRIORITY QUESTION: update_test_run_v2 exhibits the SAME field-specific dishonesty as its twin replace_test_run_v2 — updated_at is fabricated on every successful write and never persists, and overall_progress is echoed off-by-one (4 vs actual 5) on every write regardless of what was touched. The assignee mis-echo in write 1 (stale null instead of the new value) matches the direction of replace's bug (echoing pre-write state). Write 2 couldn't re-test the assignee-lie directly (old value == new value, since assignee was left untouched), but the updated_at/overall_progress lie reproduced identically and independently on both writes, and matches replace_test_run_v2's exact same three fields — this is an entity-wide write-response defect across the test-run update route family (both PATCH and POST paths), not an artifact of one endpoint or of preprod flakiness (the control run TR-9058 stayed static and self-consistent throughout; the anomaly here is a deterministic, reproduced pattern of specific fields, not a null-body/500 style transient). PRIORITY 2 — update vs replace semantics: update_test_run_v2 is genuinely SPARSE, confirmed on two independent fields across the two writes: tags ('replace-probe-tag') and description ('

replace-probe-partial-description

') were both omitted from write 1 and survived unchanged; assignee ('ing@bsstag.com', just set by write 1) was omitted from write 2 and survived unchanged rather than being cleared. This is the opposite of replace_test_run_v2, which cleared assignee to null on the same kind of omission. The two capabilities are NOT near-duplicates despite the shared route/response shape — 'update' truly means partial-merge, 'replace' truly means clear-on-omission, exactly as each one's own intent text claims. ROW SET: composition was left completely untouched by both writes (neither sent test_cases/folder_ids/configurations), and all 5 rows survived intact, including the accidental TC-54457 duplicate (latest_result_id 2150387252 and 2150387283) — consistent with the documented behaviour ('send neither and the run's composition is left completely untouched') and with replace's earlier union-preserving result on the same run. DESCRIPTION HTML WRAPPING: plain text sent to update_test_run_v2 ('update-probe-second-description') came back and persisted with NO

wrapping — unlike replace_test_run_v2, which wrapped the same kind of plain input in

tags. This is an undocumented behavioural difference between the two twins (update's own contract only says HTML is 'escaped and sanitised', not that plain text is left alone while replace wraps it) — worth flagging as a minor inconsistency in an otherwise shared contract description. is_dynamic: filter_test_cases.is_dynamic came back as boolean (false) in both update_test_run_v2 responses and in get_test_run_v2, consistent with the batch-4 finding that this route family agrees with list_test_runs_v2/get_test_run_v2 against get_test_plan_test_runs_v2's integer. DRIFT is entity-wide and already known, not new: declared-but-absent (id, uuid, owner, is_automation, top-level is_dynamic, test_plans, test_cases_count, overall_progress_by_status_id) and undeclared-but-returned (filter_test_cases, urls, links.test_cases, issues:[]) both match the standing entity-wide list; assignee declared as an object but returned as a plain string, and overall_progress declared as seven fixed lowercase keys but returned as a sparse capitalised map ({Untested:N}) — both consistent with prior findings, recorded here as confirmed-consistent rather than new.
